title: CAO 2023 performance objectives approved
subtitle: Council also updated committee appointments and endorsed Councillor Chew's bid for the Federation of Canadian Municipalities board.
overview: Council met in a closed session to discuss the 2023 Chief Administrative Officer performance objectives. It then returned to open session and approved the objectives, as amended in the closed meeting {{vote:m2}}. The CAO must now give a public presentation on those objectives at the February 7, 2023 Committee of the Whole meeting. Residents will be able to hear the objectives directly.

Council also made changes to committee roles. Councillor Richardson replaces Councillor Busuttil as Vice-Chair of Audit. A new Governance vice-chair position was created, and Councillor Busuttil was appointed to it. Councillors Downer and Klassen were named chair and vice-chair of the Committee of Management for the Elliott {{vote:m4}}.

Council endorsed Councillor Ken Yee Chew to stand for election to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors. The City will cover the costs of attending board meetings {{vote:m5}}. Council also passed four by-laws, confirmed earlier minutes and adjourned.

decisions.detail: Council approved the Chief Administrative Officer's 2023 performance objectives, as amended in closed session, and directed a public presentation on them at the February 7, 2023 Committee of the Whole meeting.
Councillor Richardson replaces Councillor Busuttil as Vice-Chair of Audit for a term ending November 15, 2024.
The Committee of the Whole terms of reference will be updated to include a Governance vice-chair, and Councillor Busuttil was appointed to the role until November 15, 2024.

decisions.item: Committee of Management for the Elliott
decisions.detail: Councillor Downer was appointed chair and Councillor Klassen vice-chair, both for terms ending November 15, 2024.
Council endorsed Councillor Ken Yee Chew to stand for election to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors through November 2026, with the City covering related attendance costs.

debate: There was little formal debate. The CAO objectives motion was moved in open session after the closed discussion, and no one raised further questions before the vote.

On the Federation of Canadian Municipalities endorsement, the Mayor asked whether anyone else wished to be considered and no one came forward. Councillors said they would support and promote the candidacy.
During the by-laws item, one councillor welcomed the removal of a holding provision on a property, saying it brings additional support one step closer.
